channel.title: Philosophy | Fred Xu
channel.description: Essays on philosophy, literature, art and life.

item.title: The Prince's Virtue, East and West
item.description: Machiavelli's princes, the tyrants of Plato's dialogues and the emperors of China feign, sacrifice their ministers, destroy their captains and kill their kin with the same small repertoire, and they weep afterwards. What divides the three traditions is who may forgive the prince, and their words for his excellence, aretē, 德 (dé) and virtù, record the same choice. Since no prince can foresee the effect by which he asks to be judged, Machiavelli's excuse fails on its own terms.

item.title: The Sash and the Suit
item.description: China's junzi, Japan's samurai and the English gentleman all began as ranks of birth that moralists claimed for character, and all three traditions spent their anxiety on the manners meant to make that character visible. The modern gentleman is those manners cut loose: a suit that can be handed down, rented with the house, or worn to seal a threat.

item.title: The Geometry of Love
item.description: Anne Carson draws desire as a triangle whose third point holds lover and beloved apart. Following her back to Sappho and Plato, this essay traces the shapes love draws in space and in time, and asks whether there is a love that is neither lack nor pure gift.

item.title: Illusions and Illusions
item.description: The Diamond Sutra cuts through illusion twice: once through the forms a mind takes to be solid, beginning with itself, and once more through the illusion of having seen through them.

item.title: The Ontology of Love
item.description: What is this thing, love, that it binds two creatures to each other in life and in death? More fundamentally, what is being-in-love, and how is it related to being-in-the-world?

item.title: The Philosophy of Boxing
item.description: Why would anyone choose to be hit in the head? Freud's death drive, Musashi's sword after the wars, and what boxing taught me about discipline, fear and flow.

item.title: Reflection on my First Boxing Bout - A Warrior's Journey
item.description: What I learned from losing my first boxing match: sacrifice, the question of why, a sunrise on a trail, and fighting as a spiritual practice.

item.title: Jim Simons, A Tribute
item.description: A tribute to Jim Simons, mathematician, codebreaker, investor and patron of science, and an inspiration of mine: on beauty, usefulness and what wealth can do for curiosity.

item.title: Coffee Shop Reflections
item.description: Why I work best among strangers in a coffee shop, and whether the Paris café of Hemingway and the existentialists is a tradition or a fantasy sold by the cup.
